name: Starter: Finnish
about: Finnish word order and endings in real, everyday sentences.

words.kuulua: to be heard; to belong (mitä kuuluu: how are you)
words.ei: not (the negative verb: en, et, ei…)
words.täytyä: to have to (minun täytyy: I have to)

mitä-kuuluu.about: Literally, what is heard? Answer with Hyvää, kiitos (fine, thanks).

anteeksi.about: To get someone's attention, or to say sorry.

concept.line: The verb's ending marks the person, so standard Finnish often leaves out minä and sinä (asun, asut, asuu), though everyday speech often keeps mä and sä.
The partitive (-a, -ä, -ta, -tä) is for amounts, objects that are partial or not definite, every object after not, and the question word mitä: lasi vettä; Juon kahvia; En juo kahvia; Mitä teet?

words.means: olen = I am; olet = you are; oletko = are you; ole = be

concept.line: Standard Finnish adds -ni or -si to the noun (siskoni, sinun nimesi, avaimeni), while everyday speech often says mun or sun without it.

words.means: minulla = minulla: with me; in my possession (minulla on = I have)
sinulla = sinulla: with you; in your possession (sinulla on = you have)
onko = onko: is ...?; is there ...? (onko sinulla ...? = do you have ...?)

concept.line: -n is of or 's (isän auto), comes before kanssa (äidin kanssa: with Mom), and marks who must: Minun täytyy lähteä.

words.means: puhutko = do you speak; puhun = I speak
ymmärrä = understand; ymmärrätkö = do you understand

concept.line: A yes/no question usually starts with the verb and -ko or -kö (Puhutko englantia?

words.means: talossa = in a house; talo = house
pienessä = in a small; pieni = small
asun = I live; asut = you live; asuu = lives
menen = I go; menet = you go; menee = goes

concept.line: Finnish says a thing is at you: Minulla on veli (I have a brother, literally at me is a brother); also feelings: Minulla on kylmä (I'm cold).

words.means: työskentelen = I work; työskennellä = to work
